properties.statement: Wrote scripts to read a month of agent session transcripts off a peer machine and count, per skill, how often it was loaded versus how often the user typed its command — then the same per tool, to compare tools whose description demands a skill against tools that demand none. The output was the evidence for two experiments about why skills go unused. Three passes were needed because the first two mis-attributed every load: the harness records tool results as user turns, and records a slash command and its expansion as two separate turns, so any naive "previous user turn" test returns a clean-looking 100% that is entirely an artifact. Nothing in the design surface reads session history, so the whole question — is the kit actually being reached for — is answerable only from outside it.
